Description and usage of MsBackendTimsTof

Source: vignettes/MsBackendTimsTof.Rmd
MsBackendTimsTof.Rmd

Introduction

The Spectra package provides a central infrastructure for Mass Spectrometry (MS) data in R. The package supports interchangeable use of different backends to represent or import MS data from a variety of formats and sources (such as mzML files). The MsBackendTimsTof” package adds support for MS data from Bruker TimsTOF raw data files. This vignette shows how, and which data can be retrieved from such files.

Installation

The package depends on the OpenTIMS C++ library to access data in timsTOF Pro data format (TDF) which is provided by the opentimsr R package. The opentimsr and MsBackendTimsTof package can be installed with:

BiocManager::install("michalsta/opentims/src/opentimsr")
BiocManager::install("RforMassSpectrometry/MsBackendTimsTof")

Some variables in the data files can only be accessed after setting up a converter library. Two options are available. The first is to use the open-source library built into opentimsr:

library(MsBackendTimsTof)

setup_converter_library()

The setup_converter_library() function is also run on package startup hence, to use the default, no manual call to setup_converter_library() is needed.

Alternatively it is possible to use the proprietary Bruker converter library, which can be downloaded and cached through BiocFileCache or downloaded to a personal folder. Note that this library is currently only available for Windows and Linux (no macOS support).

setup_converter_library(opensource = FALSE)

Accessing data from Bruker TimsTOF files

The MsBackendTimsTof package adds support for Bruker TimsTOF files to Spectra-based analysis workflows. Below we load the package which will also automatically setup the use of the open-source converter library.

library(MsBackendTimsTof)

As detailed in the installation section, the code to download the shared library would only be necessary once, if the path to this file is defined in a environment variable TIMSTOF_LIB.

We next load the TDF test file which is bundled within this package.

## Get the path/file name of the example file
fl <- system.file("ddaPASEF.d", package = "MsBackendTimsTof")

## Initialize the MsBackend
be <- backendInitialize(MsBackendTimsTof(), fl)
be
## MsBackendTimsTof with 9120 spectra
##        msLevel precursorMz  polarity
##      <integer>   <numeric> <integer>
## 1            1          NA         1
## 2            1          NA         1
## 3            1          NA         1
## 4            1          NA         1
## 5            1          NA         1
## ...        ...         ...       ...
## 9116         1          NA         1
## 9117         1          NA         1
## 9118         1          NA         1
## 9119         1          NA         1
## 9120         1          NA         1
##  ... 35 more variables/columns.
##  Use  'spectraVariables' to list all of them.

In a real use case, we would however directly load the data into a Spectra object:

sps <- Spectra(fl, source = MsBackendTimsTof())
sps
## MSn data (Spectra) with 9120 spectra in a MsBackendTimsTof backend:
##        msLevel precursorMz  polarity
##      <integer>   <numeric> <integer>
## 1            1          NA         1
## 2            1          NA         1
## 3            1          NA         1
## 4            1          NA         1
## 5            1          NA         1
## ...        ...         ...       ...
## 9116         1          NA         1
## 9117         1          NA         1
## 9118         1          NA         1
## 9119         1          NA         1
## 9120         1          NA         1
##  ... 35 more variables/columns.
##  Use  'spectraVariables' to list all of them.

We thus have access to all spectra variables within the file:

spectraVariables(sps)
##  [1] "msLevel"                 "rtime"                  
##  [3] "acquisitionNum"          "scanIndex"              
##  [5] "dataStorage"             "dataOrigin"             
##  [7] "centroided"              "smoothed"               
##  [9] "polarity"                "precScanNum"            
## [11] "precursorMz"             "precursorIntensity"     
## [13] "precursorCharge"         "collisionEnergy"        
## [15] "isolationWindowLowerMz"  "isolationWindowTargetMz"
## [17] "isolationWindowUpperMz"  "frameId"                
## [19] "ScanMode"                "MsMsType"               
## [21] "TimsId"                  "MaxIntensity"           
## [23] "SummedIntensities"       "NumScans"               
## [25] "NumPeaks"                "MzCalibration"          
## [27] "T1"                      "T2"                     
## [29] "TimsCalibration"         "PropertyGroup"          
## [31] "AccumulationTime"        "RampTime"               
## [33] "Pressure"                "file"

And the full data for spectra variables can be retrieved with spectraData:

all <- spectraData(sps)
all

The data is organized by individual spectra, all spectra measured within the same frame have the same value in the spectra variable "frameId". This also means that the scanIndex is not unique within a file, only within one frame:

sps$scanIndex |> anyDuplicated()
## [1] 182

The combination of frameId and scanIndex identifies each spectrum uniquely within the same file:

spectraData(sps, c("frameId", "scanIndex", "file"))
## DataFrame with 9120 rows and 3 columns
##        frameId scanIndex      file
##      <integer> <integer> <integer>
## 1            1       218         1
## 2            1       220         1
## 3            1       221         1
## 4            1       222         1
## 5            1       223         1
## ...        ...       ...       ...
## 9116        52       719         1
## 9117        52       723         1
## 9118        52       726         1
## 9119        52       727         1
## 9120        52       730         1

The inverse ion mobility data is provided by the "inv_ion_mobility" variable. This information can be extracted as a spectra variable (i.e., one value per spectrum):

## Get the ion mobility information
sps$inv_ion_mobility |> head()
## [1] 1.364833 1.362675 1.361597 1.360518 1.359439 1.358360

But can also be requested to be added to the peaksData(). Below we extract the full peaks data (i.e., all peaks variables for all spectra) and show the information of one selected spectrum:

## Request all supported peaks variables
pd <- peaksData(sps, peaksVariables(sps))
## Show the data for the spectrum number 10
pd[[10L]]
##      frame scan    tof intensity       mz inv_ion_mobility retention_time
## [1,]     1  228 315083        36 1221.931         1.354045       0.218626
## [2,]     1  228 315091       321 1221.975         1.354045       0.218626
## [3,]     1  228 315095       116 1221.997         1.354045       0.218626
## [4,]     1  228 315270        50 1222.967         1.354045       0.218626
## [5,]     1  228 315277        65 1223.005         1.354045       0.218626
## [6,]     1  228 315453        59 1223.981         1.354045       0.218626

Note however that "inv_ion_mobility" and "retention_time" have the same value for all peaks in each spectrum. Thus, these variables should be accessed not through peaksData(), but through spectraData() or using the $ operator or the dedicated rtime() function.

The MsBackendTimsTof is a on-disk backend, hence reading peaks and spectra variables from the original data file(s) upon request. Modifying spectra variables within the raw data files is not possible (and also not desired), but, by directly extending the MsBackendCached backend from the Spectra package MsBackendTimsTof supports changing or adding spectra variables by caching them locally within the object. Below we add a new spectra variable to the object.

## Add a new spectra variable
sps$new_variable <- seq_along(sps)

This new variable is now available within the object and can be extract like any other spectra variable.

spectraVariables(sps)
##  [1] "msLevel"                 "rtime"                  
##  [3] "acquisitionNum"          "scanIndex"              
##  [5] "dataStorage"             "dataOrigin"             
##  [7] "centroided"              "smoothed"               
##  [9] "polarity"                "precScanNum"            
## [11] "precursorMz"             "precursorIntensity"     
## [13] "precursorCharge"         "collisionEnergy"        
## [15] "isolationWindowLowerMz"  "isolationWindowTargetMz"
## [17] "isolationWindowUpperMz"  "new_variable"           
## [19] "frameId"                 "ScanMode"               
## [21] "MsMsType"                "TimsId"                 
## [23] "MaxIntensity"            "SummedIntensities"      
## [25] "NumScans"                "NumPeaks"               
## [27] "MzCalibration"           "T1"                     
## [29] "T2"                      "TimsCalibration"        
## [31] "PropertyGroup"           "AccumulationTime"       
## [33] "RampTime"                "Pressure"               
## [35] "file"
sps$new_variable |> head()
## [1] 1 2 3 4 5 6

Analogously it is also possible to change existing spectra variables. Below we shift each retention time by 10 seconds.

rtime(sps) |> head()
## [1] 0.218626 0.218626 0.218626 0.218626 0.218626 0.218626
sps$rtime <- rtime(sps) + 10
rtime(sps) |> head()
## [1] 10.21863 10.21863 10.21863 10.21863 10.21863 10.21863
